method: Independently reviewed the current rewrite snapshot only. Fully read all 113 assigned ordinary code, test, CI, script, configuration, documentation and feature-evidence files in bounded sequential chunks, rereading every truncated segment. For the two large inventories, exhaustively parsed the lockfile and capability JSON and reviewed their semantic contracts, classifications, limitations and referenced-file identities. Traced root RPC admission, request leases, immutable release/provider publication, journal recovery, ownership and privilege separation, native process cleanup, workspace/Git capture and no-replace publication, CI selection and release gates. Historical audit/fix reports were not read or used for conclusions; referenced historical artifacts were checked for existence and SHA-256 only. Executed only three focused deployment test files and read-only local structural checks; no product files were changed.

lock.method: Strict local scanner consumed every nonblank line, enforced indentation and unique keys, rejected unknown sections/fields, and matched every direct dependency to the manifest and every resolved edge to its snapshot. All package resolutions contain SHA-512 integrity. Reviewed all unique engine/platform constraints, exact overrides, and registry-only/no-hook policy. No package contents or registry advisory service were queried.

capability.method: Enumerated all method names, native surfaces, workflow mappings, classifications, statuses, group memberships and assessment texts; read each group and additional-workflow assessment and limitations. Compared every JSON method variant, stable/experimental classification and TypeScript method membership; recursively hashed all declared source/test/evidence/report references without interpreting historical audit reports. This verifies inventory coherence, not all external-service workflows.

reviewFocus: Root-only management envelope, allowlisted methods, operation UUID/digest binding, bounded receipt/request-spool admission, independent executor and stopped-cgroup cleanup.
Reviewed-source control updates, source permissions and manifests, refusal launchers, persistent start conditions, process quiescence, complete-tree swap, rollback and interrupted recovery.
Pinned tool acquisition and import, bounded archives and filesystem walks, offline build environment, quotas, single-root dependency policy and complete release verification.
Installation state and boot-enable retries, release/current/previous pointers, provider generations, host-policy preservation and separate config-check namespace.
HTTPS validation/publication/recovery, TLS generation pairing, retained identity database and encryption keys, service ownership and activity/enablement restoration.
Native UID launcher, capability/group restrictions and child cleanup; descriptor-based file access, recovery material, Git index/ref transactions and managed-worktree identity.
Targeted-test selection, coverage-gap reporting, CI identity separation, source snapshot and independent audit/full-test gates; evidence does not substitute for current platform execution.

validations.command: HARNESS_TEST_PYTHON=<bundled Python 3.12.14> node scripts/run-tests.mjs --targeted tests/deploy/test_dependency_lock.py tests/deploy/test_request_spool.py tests/deploy/test_install_recovery.py
validations.limits: Local file/transaction and substituted-system fixtures. Does not establish Linux ownership, systemd, namespaces, mounts or cross-UID behavior.
Read-only admission check; no fetch, build, installation or network operation.

validations.attempt: Import PyYAML with the bundled Python
validations.resolution: No dependency was installed. The strict generated-lock subset scanner completed the exhaustive structural review.

limitations: No assigned source or ordinary evidence file was skipped. The empty skipped array describes audit-file coverage; executed tests were limited to the three explicitly listed files.

Linux root fixtures, actual systemd service/boot behavior, cgroup cleanup, namespace isolation, loop filesystems and real native-UID/Git descriptor tests were read but not executed on this Windows host. No SSH or deployment was performed.
Full and aggregate suites were not executed. No live HTTPS issuance/login, provider billing, paid inference, external MCP, remote publication or personal configuration/home was accessed.

Existing ordinary feature evidence was assessed with its recorded limitations. Its historical passing claims were not treated as current-snapshot execution. Hashing historical references established identity/existence only.

Large lockfile and capability inventory coverage used exhaustive structural traversal plus the documented semantic checks, rather than claiming a line-by-line manual read of every repetitive hash or metadata value.
No conclusion is made about current upstream advisories or downloaded third-party package contents. Current pinned source declarations and local resolution consistency were examined.
No actionable defect was confirmed within this scope; this is a bounded review result, not proof that all product or external-service paths are defect-free.
